title: Generating AI Literacy MCQs: A Multi-Agent LLM Approach
venue: Proceedings of the 56th ACM Technical Symposium on Computer Science Education V. 2 (SIGCSE TS 2025)
extended_summary:
This paper addresses the lack of scalable and reliable assessment materials for AI literacy in K-12 education. The authors ask whether a multi-agent large language model (LLM) workflow can generate high-quality multiple-choice questions (MCQs) aligned with learning objectives, grade levels, and Bloom’s taxonomy levels.

The intervention is a multi-agent MCQ generation system built with LangGraph and OpenAI’s gpt-4o-mini model. It uses a generator agent plus critique agents for language quality and item-writing flaws, with a supervisor agent that approves or revises items iteratively. The system produced 40 AI literacy MCQs for grades 7–9.

The evaluation involved three expert K-12 AI literacy educators reviewing the generated questions with a ten-item rubric covering correctness, readability, alignment to objectives, grade appropriateness, and classroom usability. Results suggested the questions were generally clear, grammatically sound, and relevant to the intended objectives, though experts differed on Bloom’s level and grade-level appropriateness for some items. Overall, the authors conclude that the approach shows strong potential for generating pedagogically useful AI literacy assessment items, but it has not yet been tested in real classrooms or on student learning outcomes.

identified_tools.name: ChatGPT
identified_tools.description: OpenAI GPT-family large language model system used for generating and critiquing AI literacy multiple-choice questions.
identified_tools.use_case: Used within a multi-agent workflow (via LangGraph) to generate, critique, revise, and approve K-12 AI literacy MCQs aligned to learning objectives, Bloom's levels, and grade level.

quality_tier_rationale: This paper is a prototype/system description with expert judgment of generated item quality, not an empirical study of student outcomes. It does not test whether the AI tool improves K-12 reading or literacy outcomes versus business-as-usual or non-AI supports.
impact_tier_rationale: The reported results suggest the system can generate pedagogically acceptable AI-literacy MCQs, but there is no measured learner impact. Because no effect on student outcomes is reported, impact on K-12 literacy is unclear.
